subject.title: [Bug]: Slack Socket Mode ghost connections after gateway restart silently drop inbound messages

question: Should Slack Socket Mode remain warning-only for multiple active connections, or should OpenClaw add live-proven recovery/fencing for stale same-gateway restart ghosts?
rationale: The report describes real user-visible message loss, but the safe response depends on whether maintainers want automatic intervention in a Slack-supported multiple-connection topology.

options.title: Live-proof targeted recovery
options.body: Require a real Slack restart reproduction, then implement plugin-owned recovery that targets stale same-gateway ghosts without breaking intentional multi-gateway deployments.

options.title: Keep warning-only policy
options.body: Treat current diagnostics and docs as the supported behavior and continue recommending wait-and-restart, relay, separate apps, or HTTP for affected operators.

options.title: Document Socket Mode as single-gateway production only
options.body: Make production guidance stricter and route replicated Slack ingress to relay mode or HTTP instead of adding automatic Socket Mode recovery.

recommendation.title: Live-proof targeted recovery
recommendation.body: Require a real Slack restart reproduction, then implement plugin-owned recovery that targets stale same-gateway ghosts without breaking intentional multi-gateway deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Slack plugin behavior, gateway lifecycle, docs, and compatibility policy; sampled history shows broad adjacent ownership across those areas.
